entries.title: As the world churns: The streaming wars go global
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that in 2022, at least 150 million paid subscriptions to streaming video on-demand (SVOD) services will be cancelled worldwide, with churn rates of up to 30% per market.
entries.subject: Streaming video churn

entries.title: The games console: Fitter than ever at 50
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the console market will generate US$81 billion in 2022, up 10% from 2021.
entries.subject: Game consoles

entries.title: Addressable TV ads: Targeting for reach
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that addressable TV advertising, which allows different ads to be shown to different households watching the same program, will generate about US$7.5 billion globally in 2022.
entries.subject: Addressable TV advertising

entries.title: Traditional TV wanes: Television is about to dip below half of all UK video viewing
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that, in the United Kingdom, 2022 will be the final year that traditional television from broadcasters ... collectively makes up more than 50% of video viewing on all screens.
entries.metric: traditional TV share of UK video viewing
entries.subject: Traditional TV viewing (UK)

entries.title: My kingdom for a chip: The semiconductor shortage extends into 2022
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that many types of chips will still be in short supply throughout 2022 ... By the end of 2022, we predict those lead times will be closer to 10–20 weeks and that the industry will be in balance by early 2023.
entries.subject: Semiconductor shortage

entries.title: Upping the ante: Venture capital investment in chip companies reaches new highs
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that venture capital (VC) firms globally will invest more than US$6 billion in semiconductor companies in 2022.
entries.subject: Semiconductor venture capital

entries.title: RISC-y business: Could open chip standard RISC-V gain traction against dominant incumbents?
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the market for RISC-V processing cores will double in 2022 from what it was in 2021—and that it will double again in 2023
entries.subject: RISC-V

entries.title: Fixed wireless access: Gaining ground on wired broadband
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the number of FWA connections will grow from about 60 million in 2020 to roughly 88 million in 2022, with 5G FWA representing almost 7% of the total
entries.subject: Fixed wireless access

entries.title: Wi-Fi 6: Unsung, underexposed—and indispensable to the future of enterprise connectivity
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that more Wi-Fi 6 devices will ship in 2022 than 5G devices, to the tune of at least 2.5 billion Wi-Fi 6 devices versus roughly 1.5 billion 5G devices.
entries.subject: Wi-Fi 6

entries.title: Wearable technology in health care: Getting better all the time
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that 320 million consumer health and wellness wearable devices will ship worldwide in 2022
entries.metric: consumer health and wellness wearables shipped
entries.subject: Health wearables

entries.title: Mental health goes mobile: The mental health app market will keep on growing
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that global spending on mobile mental health applications will reach close to US$500 million in 2022.
entries.metric: global spending on mobile mental health apps
entries.subject: Mental health apps

entries.title: Making smartphones sustainable: Live long and greener
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that smartphones ... will generate 146 million tons of CO2 or equivalent emissions (CO2e) in 2022.
entries.subject: Smartphone carbon footprint

entries.title: Floatovoltaics enters the renewable energy mix: Floating solar panels are now commercially viable
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the aggregate installed capacity of floating photovoltaics (FPVs) ... will reach 5.2 gigawatts peak (GWp) globally by the end of 2022, representing US$4–5 billion in spending.
entries.subject: Floating solar

entries.title: The gender gap in reading: Boy meets book, boy loses book, boy never gets book back
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that boys and men in almost every country will continue to spend less time reading books, and read them less frequently, than girls and women.
entries.subject: Reading gender gap

entries.title: Women in the tech industry: Gaining ground, but facing new headwinds
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that large global technology firms, on average, will reach nearly 33% overall female representation in their workforces in 2022, up slightly more than 2 percentage points from 2019
entries.metric: female share of large tech firm workforces
entries.subject: Women in tech

entries.title: From trading cards to digital video: Sports NFTs kick sports memorabilia into the digital age
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that NFTs for sports media will generate more than US$2 billion in transactions in 2022, about double the figure for 2021.
entries.subject: Sports NFTs

entries.title: Keeping AI private: Homomorphic encryption and federated learning can underpin more private, secure AI
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that ... the combined market for HE and FL will grow at double-digit rates in 2022 to more than US$250 million.
entries.metric: homomorphic encryption and federated learning market
entries.subject: Privacy-preserving AI

entries.title: Quantum computing in 2022: Newsful, but how useful?
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that the multiple companies making quantum computers (QCs) will double their QCs' quantum volume ... from what it was in 2021.
entries.subject: Quantum computing

entries.title: AIs wide shut: AI regulation gets (even more) serious
entries.quote: Deloitte Global predicts that 2022 will see a great deal of discussion about regulating AI more systematically, with several proposals being made— although enacting them into actual enforced regulations will likely happen in 2023 or beyond.
entries.subject: AI regulation

notes: 21st edition by count from 2002. Grouped into six themes (section field). The Deloitte Insights edition URL serves the full report PDF. Publication month from the December launch pattern; exact day not confirmed. Rank is the order in the report.
